# DKR-002: Docker API is not on TCP without TLS

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** critical
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

The Docker API is root on the host. A daemon listening on TCP (conventionally 2375) without tlsverify lets anyone who reaches the port start a privileged container that mounts the host filesystem. Scanners look for 2375 all day. Even a loopback listener gives every local user and every host network container root. stackward reads the hosts in daemon.json and the effective ExecStart of docker.service, and the listening sockets on 2375 and 2376 from the shared listener facts (ss or /proc, no root needed). This check can fail without access to the Docker socket.

## Verify by hand

```sh
grep -n hosts /etc/docker/daemon.json; systemctl cat docker | grep ExecStart; ss -tlnp | grep -E ':(2375|2376) '
```

## How to fix it

Remove -H tcp:// from the unit and "hosts" from daemon.json. For remote access use DOCKER_HOST=ssh://user@host, or a socket proxy that allows only the GET endpoints needed. If TCP is truly needed, use 2376 with tlsverify and client certificates.

## What a fix can break

Tools that reach the daemon over TCP (a remote CI runner, a monitoring agent) stop working until they move to SSH or a socket proxy.
